findings.title: Unescaped URL interpolated into raw-HTML post enables stored XSS
findings.body: `TopicEmbed.import` appends `#{url}` to `contents` without any HTML/attribute escaping, and the resulting post is created with `cook_method: raw_html`, so `Post#cook` returns it verbatim and `best.html.erb` renders it with `raw`. The URL reaches this code from the anonymous `embed_url` request parameter (EmbedController -> RetrieveTopic job -> TopicRetriever -> import_remote); TopicRetriever only validates the host, and `URI()` accepts `'` in paths, so a URL like `http:///x'onmouseover='alert(1)` produces `` stored in a public topic. Escape the URL (e.g. `ERB::Util.html_escape`) or build the anchor with a helper.

findings.title: Kernel#open on remote URL relies on open-uri being loaded and follows redirects to arbitrary hosts
findings.body: `import_remote` calls `open(url).read` but `topic_embed.rb` never requires `open-uri` (only `poll_feed.rb` does). If the RetrieveTopic job runs in a process where open-uri hasn't been loaded by something else, `open` is `Kernel#open` on a filename and raises `Errno::ENOENT` for `http://...`. Additionally, even with open-uri, redirects from the (host-validated) embeddable host are followed to any destination, so a redirect to an internal address lets an anonymous user make the server fetch internal resources and publish the readability-extracted content as a topic. Use an explicit HTTP client with redirect control and require it explicitly.

findings.title: absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs
findings.body: `href.start_with?('/')` is also true for protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/img.png`, and `href.sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both slashes, producing `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/img.png`. Links and images in imported feed content that use `//host/...` form will be rewritten to broken URLs. Check `start_with?('/') && !start_with?('//')` (or use `URI.join`).

findings.title: poll_feed crashes on items without content
findings.body: `i.content.scrub` is called unconditionally. Plain RSS 2.0 items commonly have `description` but no `content` (SimpleRSS returns nil for missing fields), and Atom entries may omit it too, so `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError and aborts the entire poll (with `retry: false`), meaning no items from that feed are ever imported. Fall back to `i.description`/`i.summary` and guard nil. The unused `feed_key` method also suggests intended conditional-fetch logic that was never wired up.

findings.title: postMessage origin check uses substring match
findings.body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of `discourseUrl`; e.g. for `discourseUrl = "http://forum.example.com/"`, an origin of `http://forum.example.co` or `http://f` (any prefix) passes. Any page able to post messages to the host window can then set the iframe height arbitrarily. Compare the origin exactly against the parsed origin of `discourseUrl`.

findings.title: Already-committed migration changed to force: true
findings.body: An existing migration was edited to add `force: true` to `create_table :top_topics`. Editing a migration that may already have been applied in deployments has no effect there, while `force: true` silently drops any pre-existing `top_topics` table (and its data) on environments where the migration runs after the table exists. The same pattern is used for the new `topic_embeds` table. Prefer a new migration or drop the `force` flag.

findings.title: Test description says 404 but missing embed_url yields 400 and test only asserts non-success
findings.body: `params.require(:embed_url)` raises `ActionController::ParameterMissing`, which is rendered as 400, not 404 as the spec title claims. The assertion `response.should_not be_success` would also pass if the action raised any unrelated error (e.g. the referer check failing first), so it does not verify the intended behavior. Assert the specific status.

findings.title: Stray `end if` in ERB only works by accident
findings.body: `<%- end if %>` compiles to Ruby `end if` followed by a newline, making the next generated output statement the condition of a modifier-`if` applied to the whole header block. It happens to parse and evaluate truthy, but it is a latent syntax trap (any change to the following line can break the template). Should be `<%- end %>`.
